# `type-widened`

Type widened

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `type-widened` (both directions), `type-widened-in-request`, `type-widened-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

The type now accepts more, e.g. `integer` → `number`, or a type was added to a type array.

## Why this default

In requests: old values are still valid. In responses: clients parsing the old type (e.g. into an int) fail on the new values.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  type-widened: error
```

## How to fix

In responses, keep returning the old type.
